#!/bin/sh
set -eu
# Kathara: interfacce gia attive, solo IPv4 e routing statico.
ip -4 address show dev eth0 | grep -Fq 'inet 10.14.1.11/24 ' || ip address add 10.14.1.11/24 dev eth0

ip route replace default via 10.14.1.1 dev eth0

# ARP statico limitato ai vicini sul medesimo dominio L2.
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.1 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:01 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.12 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:03 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.13 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:04 nud permanent dev eth0
ip -4 neigh replace 10.14.1.14 lladdr 02:00:00:0a:01:05 nud permanent dev eth0

# Stabilizzazione del gateway (massimo 8 tentativi, mai fatale).
probe_attempt=0
while [ "$probe_attempt" -lt 8 ]; do
    if ping -n -I eth0 -c 1 -W 1 10.14.1.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        break
    fi
    probe_attempt=$((probe_attempt + 1))
    [ "$probe_attempt" -lt 8 ] || break
    sleep 1
done

/bin/bash -lc "cat > DNS-README.md <<'EOF'
# Lab DNS

The existing "'`kathara/base` image must provide BIND 9 (`named`) on pc1–pc14 and Python 3 on pc4. The startup scripts start BIND after configuring the existing network; pc4 also serves `/var/www/html` on HTTP port 80. The DNS files are copied into each machine using Kathara'"'s per-machine filesystem directories.

pc14 (10.14.4.14) is the recursive resolver. Its only root hint is pc1 (10.14.1.11), and recursion is allowed for the two client LANs. pc16–pc20 use pc14 in "'`/etc/resolv.conf`. DNSSEC validation is disabled because this is a private, unsigned hierarchy.

After starting the lab, run these from any client (for example, pc16):

```sh
dig @10.14.4.14 shop.example.com A +short
dig @10.14.4.14 api.service.com A +short
dig @10.14.4.14 ci.tools.net A +short
dig @10.14.4.14 ai.research.lab.net A +short
dig @10.14.4.14 data.research.lab.net A +short
dig @10.14.4.14 example.com MX +short
dig @10.14.4.14 service.com MX +short
dig @10.14.4.14 lab.net MX +short
dig @10.14.4.14 tools.net MX +short
curl http://www.example.com/
```

To inspect a referral directly, for example: `dig @10.14.3.13 ai.research.lab.net NS +norecurse`. The response should contain the child NS in the authority section and its address as glue in the additional section. Repeat with the other parent servers to inspect the hierarchy.

The MX and A records provide mail routing information. They do not install or configure an SMTP server or mailboxes.
EOF'

item.text:
Configured the 13-zone DNS hierarchy and its 12 delegations, with pc14 providing recursive resolution for pc16–pc20. The four main domains have the requested MX and mail A records, and pc4 serves a page for `www.example.com`. The existing topology, addresses and routes were left unchanged.

Static checks passed for the zone SOA and NS records, delegations, glue, MX records, client settings and startup script syntax. I could not run an end-to-end lab test because Kathara and an accessible Docker daemon are unavailable in this environment.

The [DNS README](/private/var/folders/84/zz92dr1178v8z_tvd_q2dfw40000gn/T/kathara-aut-nj5nea5p/lab/DNS-README.md) contains runtime requirements and verification commands. The mail configuration supplies DNS routing records; it does not install an SMTP server or mailboxes.
